          The Totemist

          by Ak'chamel, The Giver Of Illness

          supported by
          philipringler
          philipringler There was a time when I just stopped listening to music. I sold all my musical equipment, gave away my records, and just stopped music. That is until I randomly heard The Totemist by Ak’Chamel on KALX radio with the late great DJ Megasoup. He played Firedriver and it lit me back up, made me care about sound again, and hit all the places in my soul that needed to be awakened. Then I bought all new gear, started listening to music again, and making music. This is a powerful record. It changed me.

          about

          First vinyl release of Ak'chamel after a prolific cassette discography, The Totemist marks a new direction for the mysterious group. Equipped with studio quality recordings and a (somewhat) lighter tone, opposed to the oppressively lo-fi sound the group is known for.

          This is a deep psychedelic-folk album with hints of mysticism, some of which was written and recorded in a ghost-town in the Chihuahuan Desert in far West Texas - a place where the dead outnumber the living. Various overdubs and field recordings were captured in the historic Terlingua cemetery : an ancient burial ground filled with small grottoes and graves made of sticks and stones. This being the final resting place for miners who succumbed from illnesses derived from the toxic rare-earth element known as mercury.

          Ak’chamel, The Giver of Illness circumcising the foreskin of enlightenment and performing in homemade costumes and masks, they have played festivals in various cities around the U.S gaining international attention from Vice, The Wire, Tiny Mix Tapes, Consequence of Sound, and many more. Enter the fourth world now !
